summary: Alert Tagging: attach multiple free-form tags to an alert (many-to-many), add/remove tag endpoints, optional tag filter on list, and tags in AlertResponse.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new Tag concept exists with a many-to-many relationship to Alert, persisted via a new join table and an EF Core migration (plus matching database/*.sql scripts).
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags accepts one or more tags and adds them to the alert, returning the updated alert (with its tags).
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags dedupes tags case-insensitively so an alert never holds two tags that differ only in case, and adding an already-present tag is a no-op.
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags rejects the request (400) when the resulting tag set would exceed 10 tags per alert, or when any supplied tag is not 1-30 characters after trimming.
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags returns 404 when no alert with the given id exists.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} removes the tag assignment from the alert and returns success (e.g. 204).
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} returns 404 when the alert does not exist or the tag is not assigned to the alert (case-insensitive match).

GET /api/alerts accepts an optional 'tag' query parameter that filters alerts to those carrying that tag (case-insensitive), composable with the existing isActive, severity, CreatedFrom/CreatedTo, and search filters.
AlertResponse includes the alert's tags, and they are returned by all endpoints that return an AlertResponse (list, get-by-id, create, update, deactivate, tag add).

adjacent_dependencies: AlertService.DTO/Responses/TagOperationStatus.cs (new result enum for tag add/remove outcomes)
constraints: Follow the existing layered flow: controller -> IAlertService -> IAlertRepository; controllers never see entities, service returns DTOs only.
Tags are free-form strings; dedupe and filter case-insensitively, consistent with the existing case-insensitive Search filter.
Max 10 tags per alert; each tag 1-30 characters after trimming; centralize limits as AlertConstants (mirror existing constant pattern).
Persist the enum/collection using EF configuration classes (ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly), matching AlertConfiguration conventions; keep EF out of the service layer.
Provide both an EF Core migration and a matching hand-maintained database/*.sql script, consistent with the existing database/ scripts.
Do not change unrelated alert fields, sorting, paging, or summary behavior.
coverage_goals: Behavior coverage for tag add (dedupe, max-10, 1-30 length, 404), tag remove (success, 404 alert/assignment), tag filter composability, and tags present in AlertResponse.
unresolved_questions: Shape of tags in AlertResponse: list of plain strings (recommended, matches free-form tags) vs list of {id,name} objects — assumed plain strings unless reviewer decides otherwise.

DELETE tag route: whether the {tag} segment carries raw tag text (needs URL-encoding and a catch-all/constraint for characters like '.'/'/') or whether removal should instead take the tag in the body/query — assumed encoded path segment matched case-insensitively.
Whether Tag rows are shared/reused across alerts (unique tag name reused via join) or duplicated per alert — assumed shared unique tag names referenced by the join table.
